authorship: Angles, scope, proof banks and chapter assignments authored by Codex; prose executed through the existing configured text facade and subject to separate editorial review.
duration: 24 chapters of about 950-1080 words; target 22000-25000 words. Actual audio duration must be measured.

episodes.title: The Biggest Mysteries of the Force Explained to Fall Asleep To | Star Wars Theories
episodes.angle: Follow the limits of what characters can know about the Force. Explain shown phenomena before testing interpretations; this is neither Sith history nor another Vader biography.
episodes.scope: Canon films and the named released Clone Wars, Rebels and Ahsoka scenes. No Legends lore or unreleased answers. Mysteries means explained evidence and remaining interpretive questions, not claimed secret revelations.
forbidden: Equal numbers of Jedi and Sith as the definition of balance
Palpatine or Plagueis confirmed to have created Anakin
Abeloth, the Ones' origin, the Whills or Grey Jedi doctrine treated as canon answers
World Between Worlds as a proven unlimited time-rewrite machine
Force ghosts as a common automatic outcome for all dead Jedi
Midichlorians are the Force itself
Healing always costs a life
Sabine proves everyone has identical potential
Future Ahsoka seasons or game-only scenes
Invented dialogue and power rankings

proof.fact: The Force is created by living things; the films show perception, influence and agency without giving an exhaustive scientific account.
proof.work: A New Hope; The Empire Strikes Back; The Phantom Menace

proof.fact: Midichlorians are the symbiotic means of communication with the Force in Qui-Gon's explanation; potential and training remain different questions.
proof.work: The Phantom Menace; Ahsoka Part Three

proof.fact: Mortis presents Father, Son and Daughter; the Son shows Anakin his future and the Father removes that memory.
The Dagobah cave presents Yoda and Luke with visions; Luke sees his face under Vader's mask.
proof.work: The Empire Strikes Back; The Clone Wars Voices

proof.fact: Yoda follows Qui-Gon's voice and undergoes trials; persistence after death is a learned practice rather than simple physical survival.
The World Between Worlds has pathways between time and space; Ezra saves Ahsoka and does not save Kanan.
Rey and Ben share a dyad; healing, object transfer and Ben's final sacrifice are shown, without a universal rulebook.
Purrgil travel through hyperspace naturally; Ezra's relationship with living creatures matters to the liberation of Lothal.
proof.work: Rebels The Call and Family Reunion and Farewell

chapters.title: The fighter Yoda lifts
chapters.job: Hook on Luke failing to lift the X-wing and Yoda succeeding in Empire. Explain the gap between observable achievement, Luke's assumption about size and what this does not prove about unlimited power. Build the episode's question: how much do even skilled characters understand? The first chapter must already deliver a real explanation, not a list of coming mysteries.

chapters.title: A blood test and a spiritual field
chapters.job: Qui-Gon's blood test in Phantom Menace: distinguish the living organisms, their communication role and the Force itself. Explore what a high count can and cannot tell a teacher. Do not quantify unverified counts or turn potential into guaranteed wisdom. Link biology to the decisions adults make about the child.

chapters.title: What training can change
chapters.job: Ahsoka Part Three: Ahsoka explains talent and training while Sabine struggles; by the season-one finale Sabine can call her saber and assist Ezra. Compare this slow development with Luke's initial failures. Interpret training as attention and practice without promising equal ceilings for all beings or inventing how her training continued afterward.

chapters.title: Chirrut on the beach
chapters.job: Rogue One: the blind Guardian reaches the switch under fire. Separate Chirrut's devotion, practiced skills and what the film leaves unmeasured about sensitivity. Explain why faith cannot be reduced to an invulnerability guarantee; Baze and the deaths on Scarif give the scene its limits. No miraculous invisible shield asserted.

chapters.title: Qui-Gon pays attention to the present
chapters.job: Phantom Menace: Qui-Gon's emphasis on the living Force and his attention to Anakin. Explain the difference between sensing a person and having an infallible plan for that person's life. Use the Council's concern about fear as a concrete competing judgment. Do not retell the whole prequel plot.

chapters.title: Yoda listens to a dead teacher
chapters.job: Clone Wars Voices: Yoda hears Qui-Gon, others are doubtful, and he investigates. Explain the relationship between living beings and the wider cosmic Force as presented in this arc. Focus on the limits of institutional expertise and why a revered teacher can still learn. No Whills cosmology or external science.

chapters.title: Anakin's dreams of losing Padme
chapters.job: Revenge of the Sith: the dream, Anakin's response, his bargain and the events that follow. Separate a possible future from the actions taken to prevent it. Analyze the self-fulfilling reading while acknowledging the Force does not furnish a controlled experiment. No claim that Palpatine definitely sent the dreams.

chapters.title: Luke sees his friends in pain
chapters.job: Empire: Luke sees danger on Bespin, leaves training and finds a trap. Distinguish a genuine warning from complete knowledge of causes or outcomes. Compare Yoda's uncertainty with Luke's limited information, and the practical cost of acting early. Do not repeat the Anakin chapter's conclusion; center what a vision leaves out.

chapters.title: The face inside the helmet
chapters.job: The Dagobah cave test: Luke takes his weapons, fights the apparition and sees his own face. Compare literal prediction with a psychological warning about becoming what he fears. Retain both interpretive possibilities without declaring either the cave's proven mechanism. Its answer concerns Luke's behavior, not a solved origin story for the cave.

chapters.title: Balance without a head count
chapters.job: Return of the Jedi and the prequels: the prophecy concerns balance; Anakin saves Luke and turns against Sidious. Explain why equal numbers of factions do not follow from that story. Distinguish the Jedi as an institution from selfless action. Acknowledge later return of evil without a fabricated arithmetic law of cosmic equilibrium.

chapters.title: The Father's proposed successor
chapters.job: Mortis Overlords: the Father tests Anakin and asks him to remain to contain his children. Explain the local family situation, Anakin's unusual capability and the offered responsibility. Treat cosmic symbolism as interpretation. Don't declare these beings the creators of the entire Force or the only explanation of balance.

chapters.title: The Daughter and Ahsoka
chapters.job: Mortis Altar/Ghosts: the Daughter sacrifices herself and her remaining life helps restore Ahsoka through Anakin. Discuss what this particular transfer establishes, what it doesn't generalize, and the later visual association with Morai. Do not equate Ahsoka with a reincarnated goddess as a confirmed fact.

chapters.title: A future removed from memory
chapters.job: Ghosts of Mortis: the Son recruits Anakin using visions of his future; the Father erases those visions. Examine knowing an outcome versus being able to live with that knowledge, and the moral weakness of an offer to prevent catastrophe through domination. Distinguish erasing memory from erasing events.

chapters.title: Obi-Wan remains after death
chapters.job: A New Hope and Empire: Obi-Wan's voice and later appearance to Luke. Compare survival of personal identity with escape from physical death; his help has limits. Do not invent rules about where ghosts can appear, or claim every Jedi automatically learns it. Keep focus on teacher-student contact rather than a general afterlife sermon.

chapters.title: Yoda meets what he denies
chapters.job: Clone Wars Destiny: Yoda faces a dark reflection of himself during his trials. Explain recognition of inner fear and pride rather than the claim that he has no darkness. Differentiate acknowledging a temptation from giving it political or moral authority. No Grey Jedi doctrine or equal use of both sides as an official solution.

chapters.title: The Sith promise of continuing forever
chapters.job: Contrast Sidious's opera-house story about Plagueis with the dependent, damaged state encountered on Exegol. A character's sales pitch is not a verified biography. Distinguish bodily continuation, technological support and the selfless path shown by Obi-Wan; don't claim an exhaustive explanation of cloning or that Anakin was created by a Sith.

chapters.title: Two people share a connection
chapters.job: Last Jedi and Rise of Skywalker: Rey and Ben communicate, perceive one another's surroundings and transfer an object through their dyad. Distinguish Snoke's boast about joining them from the later dyad revelation. Explain what the scenes show without inventing its origin, frequency, romantic destiny or powers every bond must have.

chapters.title: Healing has different costs
chapters.job: Rise of Skywalker: Rey helps the wounded serpent, heals Ben, and later Ben gives his life to revive her. Compare degrees and circumstances; don't infer that any small wound demands a death, or that Anakin simply forgot an easy technique. Explain the missing knowledge and the difference between care and possession.

chapters.title: The lightsaber calls up an experience
chapters.job: Force Awakens: Rey touches the Skywalker lightsaber and has a vision; Maz offers guidance. Examine an object's association with events versus a perfect recorded archive. Do not copy dialogue, import game-only rules or assert that the saber chose Rey because of one proven bloodline mechanism.

chapters.title: A crystal chosen through the Force
chapters.job: Clone Wars The Gathering: younglings seek kyber crystals on Ilum; each faces a personal difficulty. Explain attunement and focus without crystal personality charts, arbitrary color psychology or numerical frequencies. Let the physical search and different students' obstacles carry the analysis.

chapters.title: Ezra hears living creatures
chapters.job: Rebels The Call and Lothal finale: Ezra learns to engage with purrgil and later their arrival changes the struggle with Thrawn. Connect the Force to a living ecology outside Jedi institutions. Natural hyperspace travel is shown; don't claim purrgil designed hyperdrives or obey any Force user on command.

chapters.title: A door between moments
chapters.job: Rebels A World Between Worlds: Ezra pulls Ahsoka from danger, considers rescuing Kanan, and understands that removing Kanan would destroy the rescue he achieved. Contrast intervention within the shown sequence with unlimited editing of history. Explain why causal restraint matters more than a catalogue of hypothetical resurrections.

chapters.title: Luke stands on Crait from far away
chapters.job: Last Jedi: Luke's projection delays Kylo while the Resistance escapes; Luke is physically elsewhere and dies after the exertion. The signs that the confrontation is unusual are evidence about this scene, not universal laws. Focus on the achieved rescue and Kylo's misreading; don't reduce the event to a power ranking.

chapters.title: What an unfinished explanation leaves us
chapters.job: Resolve the episode through a focused comparison of Luke lowering his weapon in Return of the Jedi and Rey's choice to help the serpent. Briefly distinguish what the Force lets characters perceive from the decisions it does not make for them. Do not recap the 23 chapters. End on one grounded quiet detail, with no future-series prediction or CTA.

episodes.title: The Secrets of Dune's Spacing Guild Explained to Fall Asleep To | Dune Lore
episodes.angle: The organization that makes imperial movement possible is itself dependent on one fragile supply. Follow the specific mechanisms of transport, secrecy and bargaining rather than retelling the Butlerian war or the entire Dune timeline.
episodes.scope: Frank Herbert's six original Dune novels. The main evidence is Dune and Dune Messiah; later novels enter only for Leto II's leverage and the later Ixian challenge. Book continuity throughout. No prequel origin story or film-specific navigator physiology.
forbidden: The Navigators magically create spaceflight without ships or propulsion
Exact prices, travel times, crew sizes or accident percentages without a cited primary passage
Every Guild employee is a mutated Navigator
Humanity had no space travel before the Guild
The Guild owns CHOAM or can order every emperor
A no-ship and a navigation machine are the same device
Norma Cenva or expanded-universe events folded into Frank Herbert's original account
Edric sees every detail of every possible future
Guild neutrality is absolute pacifism
Speculation about economics asserted as numerical canon

proof.fact: The Guild has an imperial-era monopoly over interstellar transport and uses spice-dependent limited prescience for navigation.
proof.work: Dune: Terminology, Guild material and final audience
proof.note: Independent plot/reference check; chapter analysis must be original, not a paraphrase of this page.

proof.fact: House Atreides and enemy military forces depend on Guild transport; neutrality permits transport of opposing powers rather than eliminating war.
proof.work: Dune: relocation to Arrakis, Harkonnen attack and imperial arrival

proof.fact: Fremen bribe the Guild in spice to keep observation satellites away from Arrakis, protecting their numbers and activities.
proof.work: Dune: Paul and Jessica learning from the Fremen

proof.fact: Paul's credible threat against spice production forces Guild representatives to accommodate his demands at the climax.
The Navigator Edric joins the conspiracy with the Bene Gesserit, Irulan and Scytale; his prescience conceals participants from Paul's view.
Hayt is a Tleilaxu ghola presented through the Guild as a gift to Paul. The arrangement combines several groups' interests.
proof.work: Dune Messiah: Hayt's arrival and the conspiracy

proof.fact: Leto II later controls spice distribution, subordinating the Guild; later Ixian navigation technology challenges dependence on Navigators.
proof.work: God Emperor of Dune; Heretics of Dune; Chapterhouse: Dune

proof.fact: The published Navigators of Dune concerns the expanded prequel period, which is separate from this script's original-six-book scope.

chapters.title: A fleet waiting for permission
chapters.job: Open on the Guild's dependence exposed during Dune's final confrontation: ships and military strength still need safe movement and spice. Establish what a transport monopoly means at the scale of an empire, without retelling Paul's entire victory or inventing fleet figures. Introduce the difference between appearing to control routes and controlling the condition that makes routes usable.

chapters.title: The interval between planets
chapters.job: Use the Atreides relocation to Arrakis to explain the Guild's everyday function: moving people, goods and House forces. Distinguish a House's own craft from the larger interstellar transport system. Discuss infrastructure as a practical necessity through this move, with no invented ticket arrangements or cabin scenes.

chapters.title: The ship and the Navigator do different jobs
chapters.job: Separate propulsion/transport technology from prescient selection of a safe course. Herbert's original novel does not provide an engineering manual. Explain why foresight can solve navigational uncertainty without being the engine itself; label any illustrative comparison as an analogy, not canonical physics. No quantified failure rates.

chapters.title: A human skill after the thinking-machine prohibition
chapters.job: Give only the minimum Butlerian context needed to explain why specialized human capacities matter. Compare Navigators with Mentats: foresight for routes versus trained analysis, without equating them. Do not redo the previous channel video about the war or introduce expanded-prequel founders.

chapters.title: Spice becomes a daily requirement
chapters.job: Explain melange's general geriatric, awareness and addictive properties as established in Dune, then the Guild's particularly intense navigational need. Trace the difference between political access to a commodity and physiological dependence on it. No dose, timetable, medical claim or withdrawal scene invented.

chapters.title: Edric inside his tank
chapters.job: Use the introduced Dune Messiah Navigator's altered body and spice-gas environment, without borrowing David Lynch's stage-three design as book canon. Distinguish a visible Guild representative from every member of the organization. Analyze the bodily cost of the institution's service and the distance between clients and the person making the voyage possible.

chapters.title: Why clients know so little
chapters.job: Guild secrecy in Dune: the service is familiar while the Navigators' reliance and methods remain guarded. Explain bargaining advantages of information asymmetry using clients' dependence, and distinguish this supported political inference from claims of a specific secret rulebook or omniscient surveillance network.

chapters.title: Transporting rival armies
chapters.job: Harkonnen and imperial movement through the transport system. Explain how neutrality can mean accepting opposing customers rather than stopping conflict. Distinguish logistical involvement from a verified decision to author the entire Atreides betrayal. Analyze why Houses may tolerate a carrier they cannot fully trust.

chapters.title: The price of moving a war
chapters.job: The attack on the Atreides is expensive and transport is part of its burden. Discuss the political consequences of costly deployment without numbers or invented Guild tariffs. A monopoly constrains the scale and sustainability of force; show the chain of reasoning and its limits instead of presenting a spreadsheet as lore.

chapters.title: The company and the carrier
chapters.job: Distinguish CHOAM's commercial structure, House interests, imperial authority and the Guild's transport leverage. No assertion that they are one institution or share an invented ownership hierarchy. Use a shipment's dependence on multiple organizations as a clearly labeled explanation, not an invented canonical transaction.

chapters.title: The Fremen buy an empty sky
chapters.job: The Fremen pay spice to prevent satellite observation. Explain what each side gets and what the absence of observation prevents outsiders from checking. Emphasize that the bribe protects practical activities and numbers, not that it makes Arrakis literally invisible. Avoid exact payment size.

chapters.title: What the Guild fails to understand about Arrakis
chapters.job: The Guild needs spice and tolerates concealment, while outsiders underestimate Fremen capacity. Analyze the difference between maintaining a commodity flow and knowing the ecology and society producing it. Use the satellite bargain and Fremen strength as evidence; don't invent a Guild study or claim all Guild members knew the complete worm cycle.

chapters.title: The maker behind the cargo
chapters.job: Explain only the worm-spice ecological relationship necessary to understand a supply threat. Contrast extracting today's spice with preserving the living cycle that produces future spice. Do not retell the existing sandworm video, give fabricated biology, or claim the Guild created the ecology.

chapters.title: Paul names the dependency
chapters.job: At Dune's climax Paul can credibly threaten the spice cycle. Carefully distinguish this novel threat from the film's nuclear-spice-field presentation. Explain why an Emperor's troops and the Guild's monopoly cannot settle a threat aimed at the common prerequisite. No step-by-step chemistry invented.

chapters.title: The Navigator's limited horizon
chapters.job: Contrast local safe-route prescience with Paul's wider political foresight. Both have limits. Explore why avoiding dangerous branches may favor institutional caution, as an interpretation drawn from the Guild's response rather than a universal law of Navigator psychology. No claim Paul can see everything either.

chapters.title: A new ruler still needs the carrier
chapters.job: After the imperial change, transport infrastructure remains necessary. Analyze mutual dependence rather than announcing the Guild's immediate disappearance. Paul holds spice leverage but cannot personally replace every voyage; explicitly present this as the political implication of the setting, without inventing decrees or treaties.

chapters.title: Edric joins a conspiracy
chapters.job: Dune Messiah's opening meeting: identify the participants and their distinct interests, then explain the Navigator's concealment role. Don't retell the whole assassination plot. Focus on why a group threatened by Paul takes a political risk despite its preference for continuity.

chapters.title: When foresight conceals another observer
chapters.job: Edric's prescient presence makes participants harder for Paul to see. Explain the distinction between a blind region and guaranteed operational safety. Compare concealment from foresight with secrecy from ordinary witnesses; a concealed meeting can still fail through human action. No exact theory of how prescient fields interact.

chapters.title: A gift with several owners' intentions
chapters.job: Hayt: the Guild presents a Tleilaxu ghola of Duncan Idaho. Distinguish manufacture, delivery, intended manipulation and the person Hayt becomes. Analyze why transport and diplomacy can conceal a weaponized emotional relationship. No invented Guild authority over Tleilaxu production.

chapters.title: Why the conspiracy's protection is incomplete
chapters.job: Dune Messiah: Duncan's recovered identity and Paul's unexpected choices disrupt the plot. Keep the focus on the failure of Edric's protective advantage rather than a detailed recap of Chani's death. Explain the gap between withholding information and controlling other people's decisions.

chapters.title: Leto II rations what the Guild needs
chapters.job: Move clearly to God Emperor of Dune. Explain Leto II's spice stockpile/distribution leverage and the Guild's constrained position under his long rule. No invented ration volumes, meetings or prices. Distinguish this targeted institutional account from the channel's existing full Leto biography.

chapters.title: Ix offers a different kind of navigation
chapters.job: Later original novels introduce navigation technology reducing the need for spice-dependent Navigators. Explain the competitive pressure of an alternative method; distinguish machines that navigate from no-ships that conceal themselves from prescience. Do not claim all Navigators instantly vanish or import expanded-sequel events.

chapters.title: An empire with more ways to move
chapters.job: Consider the later diversification of travel in relation to the original monopoly. State known setting changes briefly, then analyze resilience when no single carrier or spice allocation can immobilize everyone. Avoid unsupported numbers for the Scattering, named destinations or a complete future history.

chapters.title: The person a passenger never meets
chapters.job: End with the specific contrast between a client's apparently routine departure and Edric's dependent bodily existence. Resolve the title: Guild secrets are the practical dependencies hidden behind a reliable service. No all-chapter summary, future prediction or generic control slogan. Last detail must remain grounded in the book's tank and spice environment.

episodes.title: The Entire Story of Paul Atreides Explained to Fall Asleep To | Dune Lore
episodes.angle: A biographical reading of Paul across Frank Herbert's first three novels: how the training and alliances that save him gradually restrict the life he can choose. Distinguish achievement, responsibility and his later refusal of the path his son accepts.
episodes.scope: Dune, Dune Messiah and Children of Dune, with major book spoilers announced. The entire story means Paul's life as told in those three original novels. No expanded prequels, fictional intervening adventures, or scene details imported from the films.
forbidden: Chani leaves Paul at the end of the original Dune novel as in the 2024 film
Alia is unborn during the novel's final confrontation
Paul never makes choices because prescience controls his body
The first infant Leto and the later twin Leto II are the same child
Paul completes the Golden Path himself
Irulan's actions are harmless or Chani's pregnancy has one simple cause
Paul knows every possible future without blind spots
Ghanima dies or becomes the worm emperor
Invented dates, private thoughts, quotes, childhood adventures or exact battle statistics
Paul of Dune events merged without labeling them

proof.fact: The official original-series description introduces Paul, House Atreides' destruction and his rise on Arrakis.
proof.access_note: Search result description read; direct page returned an error. Not claimed as a fully read novel.

proof.fact: Paul is trained by Jessica, Gurney, Duncan and Thufir, survives the betrayal, joins the Fremen and rises to the imperial throne.
The novel has a first child of Paul and Chani who dies, a born Alia at its climax, and a political marriage to Irulan alongside Paul's relationship with Chani.
Dune Messiah follows Paul's reign, conspiracy, Hayt's arrival, the stone burner, Chani's death and the birth of twins.
Paul loses his physical eyes but initially continues using prescience; after events surrounding the twins he walks into the desert in the Fremen tradition.
The twins are Leto and Ghanima; Children of Dune begins after Paul's desert disappearance with Alia as regent.
The Preacher is Paul. He condemns the religion built around his name, encounters his son and is killed near the end.
Leto II accepts a transformative future that Paul could not accept. This is the endpoint of Paul's biography, not a second full God Emperor biography.

chapters.title: The emperor who walks away
chapters.job: Hook briefly on the physically blind Paul leaving his throne for the desert in Dune Messiah, without recreating novel prose. Promise a life explained through how his victories narrow his options. Announce first-three-novel spoilers. Return to his upbringing by the end of the chapter; don't give the whole ending twice.

chapters.title: A childhood prepared by several teachers
chapters.job: Caladan and the different educations provided by Jessica, Gurney, Duncan and Thufir. Explain political heir, Bene Gesserit training and developing mental discipline as distinct preparations. No invented lessons, dates, conversations or claim he has already become a fully certified Mentat.

chapters.title: Jessica's decision and the box
chapters.job: Jessica bears a son contrary to the sisterhood's intended match; Mohiam tests Paul with the pain box and gom jabbar. Explain the test's purpose from the Bene Gesserit viewpoint without endorsing its cruelty as objective science. Distinguish Paul's potential from the sisterhood's ability to control him.

chapters.title: An inheritance on a dangerous planet
chapters.job: The move from Caladan to Arrakis, Leto's awareness of political danger, and the value of spice. Explain why accepting an apparent elevation places the family inside a trap. Keep the Guild and CHOAM explanation short to avoid duplicating the separate Guild episode.

chapters.title: What Leto teaches through a rescue
chapters.job: The spice-harvester rescue in the original novel shows Leto prioritizing workers over equipment; Paul encounters spice and a different kind of political leadership. Explain practical loyalty and the cost of ruling from incomplete information. No film-only dialogue or invented cockpit details.

chapters.title: A trusted doctor opens the way
chapters.job: Yueh's betrayal under Harkonnen coercion, the destruction of House Atreides' position and Duke Leto's death. Distinguish trust in conditioning from actual knowledge of Yueh's situation. Paul's survival is contingent and assisted; don't make it proof he foresaw every tactical step.

chapters.title: Mother and son beyond the household
chapters.job: Paul and Jessica's escape into the desert, survival discipline and Paul's expanding awareness. Include his recognition of the Harkonnen family connection as a troubling change in identity, without importing the movie's timing. Explain how a lost political identity coexists with inherited training.

chapters.title: Meeting people prepared to recognize him
chapters.job: The Fremen encounter, Jessica's abilities, the Missionaria Protectiva's planted religious expectations and Paul gaining protection within them. Distinguish useful legend from proof of divine design. Fremen choices and competence remain active forces; they are not a passive crowd waiting for him.

chapters.title: Jamis and the burden of admission
chapters.job: The novel's duel with Jamis and its consequences, Paul's first killing in this context and the community's treatment of the dead. Analyze admission into a society whose customs he must learn. Avoid close recreation of the funeral scene or invented interior monologue; emphasize the relationship and responsibility that follows.

chapters.title: Usul and Muad'Dib
chapters.job: The names Paul receives/chooses and the separation between his place in a sietch and the public name people will rally around. Explain what belonging asks him to change and what political heritage he keeps. No etymological embellishment or claim he instantly understands every Fremen practice.

chapters.title: Chani and a life that might have been private
chapters.job: The original novel's relationship with Chani, their partnership and their first infant son Leto. State clearly this child is not the later twin Leto II. Explain the tension between intimate life and the movement growing around Paul, without inventing domestic scenes or repeating film Chani's later objections as book dialogue.

chapters.title: The worm and the community's expectations
chapters.job: Paul learns Fremen desert practices and rides a sandworm. Explain the concrete achievement and why meeting expectations raises the pressure to become their political/religious leader. Avoid a full sandworm biology digression or claiming a single ride grants universal authority automatically.

chapters.title: The Water of Life changes his horizon
chapters.job: Paul's dangerous transformation through the Water of Life and Chani's role in helping him recover. Differentiate increased awareness from omniscience, and his ability from the Bene Gesserit's intended obedient outcome. No dosage, biochemical instructions, or invented universal law of male physiology.

chapters.title: Winning Arrakis and losing a child
chapters.job: The final military and political struggle, death of the first infant Leto, Alia's role as an already born child, Paul's confrontation with Feyd-Rautha and spice leverage. Keep detail at biographical significance, not a blow-by-blow battle. Clearly use novel continuity rather than the films.

chapters.title: Irulan's marriage and Chani's position
chapters.job: The political settlement with House Corrino and Paul marrying Irulan while remaining committed to Chani in the novel. Discuss dynastic legitimacy versus the household relationship, with consequences for all three people. Do not present the 2024 film's departure as the novel ending or excuse Paul from choosing the arrangement.

chapters.title: A victory followed by an empire-wide war
chapters.job: Move explicitly into Dune Messiah's later reign. Explain the holy war's consequences and Paul's responsibility without reciting disputed casualty statistics or claiming he personally commands every act. Distinguish seeing a movement's danger from escaping accountability for using that movement.

chapters.title: Enemies learn to hide from a prophet
chapters.job: The conspiracy involving Edric, Mohiam, Irulan and Scytale. Explain the blind-spot problem from Paul's position, with individual motives distinguished. Do not assume he knows every conversation or restate the separate Guild episode's institutional argument.

chapters.title: Duncan returns as Hayt
chapters.job: The emotional and political arrival of the ghola. Explain why Paul accepts a presence he knows may be dangerous, and the uncertainties of memory and identity. Hayt's recovered Duncan identity matters through his choice; do not frame him as a simple perfectly obedient replacement.

chapters.title: A household entangled in succession
chapters.job: Irulan's contraceptive intervention, Chani's attempts to become pregnant and the resulting vulnerability of the family. Avoid a single-cause medical explanation or absolving the conspirators. Center how dynastic plans intrude on private decisions and how Paul faces futures he cannot comfortably reconcile.

chapters.title: Seeing without physical eyes
chapters.job: The stone burner takes Paul's sight; for a time he follows the future he perceives. Explain why this ability imposes dependence on a particular anticipated sequence, and why walking through a familiar future differs from unlimited awareness. No invented exact mechanics of the weapon.

chapters.title: The twins and the choice to leave
chapters.job: Chani dies giving birth to Leto and Ghanima; Scytale's threat is defeated, Hayt is Duncan again, and Paul relinquishes imperial life and walks into the desert. Explain his conformity to a Fremen practice and the unresolved costs left to his children. No claim the novel guarantees he is dead at this point.

chapters.title: A preacher challenges Muad'Dib's religion
chapters.job: Move explicitly to Children of Dune. The blind Preacher is eventually identified as Paul; he opposes the religious/political order around Alia. Explain the discrepancy between the man and the image used by institutions. Do not assume his critique undoes the war or makes him free from his past.

chapters.title: The future his son accepts
chapters.job: Paul's encounter with Leto II and their disagreement over the terrible path ahead. Describe Leto's transformation only as necessary to understand Paul's refusal; no second Leto biography. Acknowledge both Paul's moral limits and the costs of declining, without declaring his son objectively justified in all later acts.

chapters.title: The end of the man behind the name
chapters.job: The Preacher's killing in Children of Dune completes Paul's personal life while his public name persists. Offer the episode's biographical conclusion through that particular divergence, not a recap or generic warning about heroes. End with a grounded contrast between his presence as a person and the institutional image that survives him.
